title: video.presence.usage_rollup_by_month
description: The month-by-month shape of video.presence.usage_rollup — the table a workspace-administration screen draws. Input: {"scope_key": string, "months": integer (default 6, clamped to 1..36), "tz": string}. Response: {"scope_key": string, "tz": string, "months": [{"month": "YYYY-MM", "period_start": string, "period_end": string, "users": [ ...usage_rollup rows... ]}]}, NEWEST MONTH FIRST — the order the answer is read in, since a usage table opens on the month somebody is currently living in. Buckets are calendar months in `tz` (default UTC) and their boundaries are LOCAL midnight, so across a DST transition exactly one month is an hour short or an hour long; that is the point, since a report titled "March" must neither include the hour that belongs to April nor drop the one that belongs to March. A month with no calls is present with an empty `users` list rather than omitted: a gap meaning "no calls" must not be indistinguishable from a gap meaning "this row failed to load". `months` is clamped because the walk is linear in the spans of every bucket and the parameter is reachable from a query string.

scope_key.description: The partition to report on, as stamped on the spans.

months.description: How many calendar months back (default 6, clamped to 36).

tz.description: IANA time zone the month buckets are cut in (default UTC).
